thread:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV2 - Elevated error rates and 5xx tail on customer Jupiter Corp (enterprise VPC) in eu-west-2. PagerDuty: oncall-alex. Please acknowledge. :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: acked. grabbing context. what upstream symptoms?

sre-maria: seeing sustained 5xx from the dedicated pool serving jupiter-vpc-3. spikes started ~2m ago. latency spikes on long-running streams and some token generation timeouts.

netops-devon: noticed we started seeing increased SYN retries to edge-gw-euw2-02 for that tenant's VIP. Could be a host flapping or backend drain.

pm-elaine: customer success Ryan is on call with Jupiter — they report partial rate limiting and intermittent 502s in their dashboards. No full outage yet but impact on billing pipelines.

customer-success-ryan: confirming. their internal logs show retries and upstream DNS resolution defaults to older VIP for a subset of requests. They can tolerate brief failover but need a clean cutover.

solutions-zoe: proposing we isolate tenant to a warm pool in eu-west-2, reduce DNS TTL, and then flip VIP to warm nodes. Can we get warm capacity ready?

infra-jin: warm pool has reserved capacity (dedicated-warm-pool-jupiter). currently 60% free. I can spin instances to 100% and bring up services.

oncall-alex: action list: 1) confirm isolation rules (netops) 2) prep warm nodes (infra) 3) lower DNS TTL to 20s (dns-admin) 4) plan VIP swap and monitor 5) keep customer updated. Who takes netops?

netops-devon: I'll take netops. First step: apply iptables hold to prevent cross-tenant egress on the flapping hosts and reroute DNS for the VIP when ready. Doing quick check of route table entries.

netops-devon: running check: ```
# get current VIP targets
curl -s https://internal-dns/euw2/jupiter-vip | jq .targets
# verify edge health
ssh edge-gw-euw2-02 'sudo journalctl -u gateway -n 200 | tail -n 50'
```

sre-maria: I see a pattern where longer tokens are hitting a kernel path that's OOMing on that host. Reproduced with local load: KV cache pressure + sporadic leak in runtime. Will patch or kill the process on flapping machines.

infra-jin: starting scale-up of warm pool: `infra scale warm-pool-jupiter  --region eu-west-2 --to 8` 

infra-jin: warm nodes booting, expected ready in ~90s. health checks will auto-register.

netops-devon: I've staged the isolation ACLs to block the problematic host set: `net-ctl isolate --tenant jupiter --hosts "10.14.8.21,10.14.8.22"` Waiting for infra to confirm warm endpoints.

dns-admin: lowering TTL for jupiter-vip.eu-west-2 from 300 to 20s now. NOTE: this is on our edge DNS authoritative; changes should propagate in ~20s after update.

customer-success-ryan: telling customer we're lowering TTL and will do a controlled VIP flip to warm nodes; asking them to queue critical jobs until we confirm stability.

sre-maria: I patched the runtime on the two flapping hosts and restarted the runtime. Initial metrics look better. But I still want to move traffic to warm pool to be safe.

infra-jin: warm nodes are healthy and registered: endpoints: `10.20.4.11,10.20.4.12,10.20.4.13,10.20.4.14`. Load balancer backends show healthy.

netops-devon: prepping VIP swap. Plan: 1) shift 25% traffic via weighted LB to warm IPs 2) monitor 5xx/latency for 2 minutes 3) if ok, increase to 50% then 100% 4) drain old hosts. Will use gradual weights to avoid customer disruption.

oncall-alex: post the exact commands you will run so we have auditability.

netops-devon: commands: ```
# set LB weights
lbctl set-weight jupiter-vip euw2 10.20.4.11=25 10.14.8.21=75
# increase
lbctl set-weight jupiter-vip euw2 10.20.4.11=50 10.14.8.21=50
# final
lbctl set-weight jupiter-vip euw2 10.20.4.11=100 10.14.8.21=0
```

sre-maria: starting canary now. watch metrics on grafana panel `jupiter-vpc-3` and `/svc/jupiter/latency` dashboards. I'll watch for 5xx rate and error class spikes.

[~2m later]

netops-devon: canary 25% set. no large spike; 5xx reduced by ~40% on canary paths.

sre-maria: agree. 5xx on warm backends is low. increasing to 50%.

netops-devon: set to 50%. monitoring...

pm-elaine: customer on call says their pipelines retry and success rate improved for the canary shard. good signal.

sre-maria: increasing to 100%.

netops-devon: final weight set to warm nodes; old hosts now 0 weight. initiating drain commands: `lbctl drain jupiter-vip --hosts 10.14.8.21,10.14.8.22`

sre-maria: drain progressing. connections on old hosts falling to zero. Starting post-swap checks: token generation latency, stream stability, KV cache hit rates.

dns-admin: TTL change finished earlier; since TTL was low, external caches have picked up the new VIP mapping.

customer-success-ryan: customer confirms production traffic looks normal now. They saw reduced errors and no data loss. They asked about next steps and root cause.

oncall-alex: great. next steps: 1) keep warm pool at higher capacity for 2 hours 2) collect logs and runtime heap profiles from the old hosts for RCA 3) follow-up ticket to implement runtime memory guardrails for that model shape. Assigning RCA to sre-maria and infra-jin.

sre-maria: acknowledging RCA. I'll collect heap profiles and open an eval against the workload.

infra-jin: I'll keep warm pool at 100% for 2 hours and then scale to steady-state with alert thresholds.

pm-elaine: I'll coordinate customer comms: summary, impact, ETA for RCA.

solutions-zoe: recommend adding a per-tenant circuit-breaker in routing policy to automatically siphon traffic in these cases. I'll draft a proposal.

incident-bot: Incident update: SEV2 -> mitigated. Primary impact removed for Jupiter Corp. Please follow RCA playbook and tag tickets with `sev2-jupiter-1765432109`.

oncall-alex: closing the active paging loop. if any regressions, re-open thread or page. thanks team :thumbsup:

customer-success-ryan: thanks everyone, especially infra/jun and netops team. customer very appreciative.

sre-maria: uploading profiles and logs to the incident folder now.

netops-devon: removing temporary ACLs after drain completed.

dns-admin: TTL restored to 300 after 30m of stable traffic.

oncall-alex: final note: we did a controlled VIP swap and warm-pool migration rather than emergency DNS tear-down. documented steps under /incidents/1765432109-runbook.md

customer-success-ryan: marking customer update sent. thread resolved from CS side.

incident-bot: Incident closed at ts:1765432187."
